newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW -- UK April/May trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- UK April/May trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' reactions to UK data showing an April global trade deficit of 961 million stg vs 671 million in April and a May non-EU trade deficit of 563 million stg vs 425 million:

"The UK trade data are mixed, with the global shortfall on the high side, but the non-EU gap well below expectations. The disappointing global deficit in April conceals a solid bounce in exports, however, so only import strength was responsible for the deterioration. This should be seen as supportive of higher interest rates to cap domestic demand.

"The May non-EU shortfall was a relatively low 563 million stg. Within this, exports weakened but retraced only some of their April surge. To this end, the data continue to indicate only a limited impact upon competitiveness of the pound's climb. Worse news will inevitably come as current hedging runs out, but the overall tone of the trades so far is not worrying. Data neutral for the pound and small negative for gilts on enhanced rate hike implications."

"Worse than expected on the global side. It's premature to herald this as being the start of the deterioration of the trade balance, but there are definite signs of weakness in export volumes growth at the moment. Lot of strength on the EU side in imports. That is a sign of the strength of domestic demand, also of how competitive imports are at the moment."
